text:
incident-bot: SEV2 — elevated 502/503 errors observed for Private VPC customers routing cross-region (eu-west1 -> us-central1) via GCP internal LB. Alert threshold breached: 5m error rate 6.7% (baseline <0.5%). Paging oncall.sara-platform-oncall. :rotating_light:

observability-bot: Spike started ~2056789000. See dashboards: https://obs.redwood.example/d/route-errors?from=2056788800&to=2056789800 — early signal: token-exchange failures from GCP auth proxy in front of ILB control plane. Sample error: `auth_proxy: 401 invalid_token` then 503 downstream.

sara-platform-oncall: I'm on it, ack. Starting triage. Which customers impacted?

jess-support: Support queue shows ~17 unique Private VPC customers with >20 failed requests each; first page from EU-hosted apps. Escalated two paying enterprise customers (acct-832, acct-1902). Notified them that we're investigating.

mike-network-eng: Adding context — cross-region fanout path uses GCP ILB control plane to program forwarding rules in us-central1 for eu-west1 sessions. If control plane token exchange to internal auth fails we see synthetic 5xx on establish.

anita-infra: Reproduced a consistent 401 in our control-plane logs when trying to call `https://gcp-controlplane.internal/token` from control-plane-proxy replica 3. Stack trace snippet:```
2026-03-14T10:05:12Z control-proxy error token_exchange failed status=401 body="invalid_grant: Token exchange returned 401"
```

mike-network-eng: Is this a quota or an auth rotation? Could be GCP's token service throttling or a bad refresh token. I can query the token service logs.

observability-bot: Correlating: increased 401s from `gcp-auth-proxy` across eu-west1->us-central1 path started ~2056788950 and matches GCP API error 403/429 before that for a short window.

sara-platform-oncall: Steps: 1) apply temporary routing policy to prefer local regional endpoints for affected Private VPCs; 2) open ticket with GCP support; 3) notify customers of temporary mitigation. Who can flip the routing policy?

mike-network-eng: I can push a targeted route policy to affected projects to avoid cross-region fanout. Doing a scoped change for acct-832 and a canary acct-1902 first. Command:```
bash
# scope by project tag and set routing=regional-fallback
./infractl routing set --project-tag acct-832 --policy regional-fallback --reason "mitigate gcp token-exchange 401"
```
Applying now to acct-1902 (canary).

anita-infra: I'll also increase token refresh retry backoff in control-proxy to reduce thrash: config patch applied to replica set, rollout paused to verify. Patch:```
control-proxy:
  token_refresh:
    retries: 6
    backoff_ms: 1200
```
Rolling out to 2/3 replicas.

gcp-support-bot: GCP ticket created: INC-998271. GCP responded initial ack, investigating internal IAM/token service logs. ETA 30–60m for root cause.

lucas-product: Customer comms: we need an incident status update for the two escalated accounts. Jess, can you send a brief note referencing mitigation and ETA?

jess-support: On it. Drafting: "We're seeing intermittent 5xx for cross-region Private VPC traffic. We're applying a temporary regional routing policy while we work with GCP. No data loss expected; sessions may route to regional endpoints. Will update in 30m." Sending now.

sara-platform-oncall: Canary acct-1902 looks healthier after policy flip — error rate fell from 7.1% -> 0.8% in 5m. Rolling to the other affected customers in batches of 5. Monitoring for side effects (latency upsell).

mike-network-eng: Noted that this is a behavioral change: we prefer local region which increases egress within region but keeps traffic up. This is acceptable temporary tradeoff. Continuing rollout.

observability-bot: After rollout batch1 (5 customers), aggregated error rate for affected cohort dropped to 0.6%. Latency delta: +12ms median, p95 +58ms.

anita-infra: Control-proxy token error persists on the remaining replica (replica #1). I've pulled the token cache and see refresh failures: `oauth: refresh failed status=401 scope=compute` — tokens appear to be rejected by GCP.

mike-network-eng: I've requested a scoped token refresh trace from GCP support attached to INC-998271. Also verifying service account key rotations in customer projects — nothing suspicious yet.

sara-platform-oncall: Escalate to SRE lead for postmortem and paging if GCP ETA slips. @mike-network-eng taking lead on mitigation and liaising with GCP?

mike-network-eng: Affirmative. I'll maintain the routing rollback runbook ready to revert once GCP fixes root cause. Runbook snippet:```
# revert
./infractl routing set --project-tag <acct> --policy global-fanout --reason "restore post-gcp-fix"
```

anita-infra: Adding a metric alert to detect token-exchange 401 spike and auto-run one-step mitigation (regional pin) for small cohorts. Will follow up in changelog.

gcp-support-bot: GCP reply: internal IAM service experienced a transient auth proxy condition in region eu-west1 which caused token validations to intermittently fail. They are rolling a fix. No change required on customer keys. Monitor for reversion.

lucas-product: Good. Can we estimate customer minutes impacted and severity for post-incident report? Jess, can you pull count of failed requests per account and duration?

jess-support: Pulling now. Quick numbers: total failed requests ~32k across 17 accounts over 35m window. Top two customers saw session errors impacting web API endpoints; both on low-latency SLAs. I'll attach support logs to the incident ticket.

sara-platform-oncall: GCP reports fix rolling, I'm keeping the routing policy in place until metrics show stable baseline for 30m. If error rate stays <0.5% for 30m, we'll begin gradual rollback on a per-account basis.

observability-bot: At 2056790200, global error rate for the cohort is 0.4%. Continue monitoring.

mike-network-eng: Preparing a short postmortem owner and action items: 1) add automated failover policy that triggers regional pin when auth-proxy 401s exceed threshold; 2) increase token-service retry/backoff by default; 3) test GCP IAM proxy failure modes in chaos lab. Assigning myself as owner.

sara-platform-oncall: Handoff — my oncall shift ends at 2056790600 UTC. Handoff to anita-infra. Anita, are you good to own until resolution and postmortem kickoff?

anita-infra: I will take it. I'll stay on call and continue monitoring rollback readiness. I'll also coordinate the post-incident follow-up with mike and jess.

mike-network-eng: Noted. I'll keep liaison with GCP support until they confirm full rollback. If GCP resolves, we'll do staged rollback to global-fanout with one-account canary, then widen.

gcp-support-bot: Update from GCP: fix deployed, auth proxy error back to baseline at 2056790450 UTC. They recommend waiting 10m then validate.

anita-infra: Starting canary rollback on acct-1902 at 2056790500. Monitoring.

observability-bot: Canary rollback metrics: p50/p95 latency within 3ms/12ms of pre-incident baseline, error rate stable at 0.2% for canary. Proceeding to next batch.

sara-platform-oncall: Final status: Mitigated. Root cause: transient GCP IAM/auth proxy issue causing token exchange 401s affecting ILB control-plane cross-region programming. Impact: ~17 Private VPC customers experienced increased 5xx for cross-region flows for ~35m. Mitigation: applied temporary regional routing policy to affected customers, increased token retry/backoff. GCP acknowledged and fixed their proxy.

lucas-product: Assign postmortem owner: mike-network-eng. Action items: automated detection + mitigation playbook, token-retry defaults, chaos testing on GCP auth path. Timeline: draft postmortem in 3 business days.

jess-support: Sent final customer updates to impacted accounts. Two key customers requested a follow-up call; scheduling with SEs.

anita-infra: I'll keep the routing policy in place until 30m of baseline after full rollback, then revert and monitor. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident cleared (SEV2 -> resolved) at 2056790523. Incident record: INC-998271.
